samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one row of equal solid coloured squares, evenly spaced and standing side by side, and exactly one further solid coloured square of the same size standing on its own well above that row. Every pale grey mark anywhere in the picture is inert decoration that means nothing. Each coloured square is a bead, and every bead is red, green, blue or yellow. The lone bead above the row is the one bead that is already lying in the pan. The pan itself is not drawn, and the beads that collect in it are never drawn, so you must keep track of the pile in your head. The beads of the row are the queue, and they are tipped into the pan one at a time in order, starting with the leftmost bead of the row and finishing with the rightmost. Tipping one bead in works like this: if the bead now showing on top of the pan is the same colour as the arriving bead, the two wipe each other out and both are removed from the pan, uncovering whatever lay beneath; otherwise the arriving bead simply comes to rest on top of the pan and covers what was there. The pan never becomes empty at any point, and no bead ever enters the pan except by being tipped in from the row, in that left-to-right order. After the whole row has been tipped in, which colour is showing on top of the pan? Answer with one of red, green, blue or yellow.
